description: MonkeyMode guardrail preset: Unity (C#) + Mirror networking. Applies to files under scopeRoot. Rules marked [Mirror] only matter for Mirror projects; delete them if you do not use Mirror. Changing this file needs user approval (docs/ai/12_GUARDRAILS_INSTEAD_OF_COMMENTS.md).

rules.message: Tween libraries are banned. Their lifetime problems keep recurring: callbacks run after the target is destroyed and tweens leak. Drive state changes with Animator, AnimationCurve or a state machine; when server state is the cause, change only the presentation in the SyncVar hook. See docs/ai/13_BANNED_APIS.md
APIs that call methods by string name are banned. Renaming breaks them with no compile error. Use an interface call or a C# event/delegate.
String- or nameof-based Invoke/StartCoroutine is banned. Start coroutines with an IEnumerator argument and give each one a single lifetime owner.

Scene-wide lookups are banned. They create hidden dependencies on hierarchy shape and load order and break at network spawn time. Use serialized inspector references, injection at creation, or a registration-based registry.
Loading from Resources is banned. It depends on string paths and bloats the build. Use serialized references or a ScriptableObject registry.
async void is banned. Callers cannot catch its exceptions and it keeps running after the object is destroyed. Return Awaitable or Task and pass destroyCancellationToken, or use a coroutine.
Creating Thread directly is banned. Unity APIs are only safe on the main thread and stray threads survive shutdown. Use Awaitable.BackgroundThreadAsync or the Job System.
Runtime reflection is banned. It severs static references, so IL2CPP stripping and refactors break it silently. Use an interface or a registration table.

Calling Debug.Log directly is banned. Agents judge behavior from logs, so every line needs a consistent category and level. Use your project's logging wrapper (for example <AssemblyPrefix>Core.Logging.Log.Info/Warn/Error(category, message)).

[Mirror] Commands with requiresAuthority = false are banned. Any client could send requests for objects it does not own. Send the Command from a player-owned object, pass the target NetworkIdentity, and validate distance, ownership and ability on the server.
Assigning Time.timeScale is banned in networked games. Server and client clocks drift apart and physics sync breaks. Pause with a server-side gate flag and a single session clock.
